limitations: Models owner-fence decisions exactly. Authentication itself and asynchronous cleanup requested by revoke belong to gateway models.
Two owners, five request sequence values, arbitrary epoch offsets around the current epoch.
Quint ITF traces are replayed through the real implementation by packages/scripts/quint/check-application.ts. This checks sampled trace conformance, not unbounded refinement.

Finite verification domain. Two owner identities, epochs 0..3, sequences 0..4, started epoch current-1/current/current+1. Values beyond these bounds are outside this instance; generation and revision values never wrap.
One startup, four optional returned resources, one connected HTTP request, an external close and one joined managed close. The close receipt follows request drain before reverse-order release begins.

A real Node HTTP/file fixture checks a held request during both close paths, reverse-order release, startup rollback and release failures. Fair progress assumes request settlement, the close event and all release continuations.
Unreturned partial acquisitions, close while a factory is unresolved, forced shutdown, upgraded sockets, concurrent request sets and work that outlives a disconnected client remain outside the model.
One already admitted handle, one serial read or autocommitted write, two owner checks, two close attempts and one closed-handle use. Owner decisions are host inputs.

Refusal before dispatch prevents an effect. Refusal after a completed native call suppresses the result while a committed write survives. Native exceptions leave effects unknown. An acknowledged close retires the handle, and an unacknowledged close may be retried.

The strict fixture uses the adapter with a controlled loader and real local SQLite persistence. Key custody, authentication, native encryption and lease behavior, multi-statement transactions, reentrant calls and platform qualification remain outside this proof.

One queue handle with at most two rows, three event IDs, one checkpoint, one pending upload and one clean reopen. An exact durable reply can remove only the captured IDs. Withdrawal clears the queue and checkpoint and persists after a late reply.

Existing real SQLite cases cover encrypted retention across reopen, exact reply checking, withdrawal, serialization and overflow. A controlled sender supplies replies. Fair progress assumes settlement of the admitted callback and its local continuation.
Producer capture and cancellation, collector authority, database leases, timer policy, multiple handles, arbitrary storage faults and crash durability remain separate.
